text: Geo-replication replicates data but leaves a problem unsolved: how does the application know which region is primary? A failover group adds a stable listener endpoint Azure always points at the current primary.

With geo-replication alone, the client must know the actual server name, updated by hand after a failover. A failover group adds one stable endpoint plus an optional automatic failover policy on top of the same replication.
Failover can be manual, same control as plain geo-replication, or automatic with a grace period — how long to wait before triggering, so a brief blip doesn't cause an unnecessary failover.
Creating one is a PowerShell or CLI operation, not T-SQL, since a failover group is a server-level resource. Afterward the application connects to one stable name, never the individual servers.
Geo-replication moves the data; a failover group also moves where the application points. Next up: log shipping — an older mechanism, still used in hybrid on-prem-to-Azure scenarios.
